headline: High-risk shared filesystem and broad egress make n8n→TREK prompt injection, leakage, and cascading action errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: n8n can read/write the server filesystem and orchestrates tools via workflow nodes; TREK uses MCP and real-time collaborative inputs. That creates a plausible content-bridging path where attacker-controlled travel data or files can be treated as instructions. The interaction is documented only at profile level, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF n8n workflows ingest TREK-generated files or MCP-fed content as prompts
IF TREK exposes user-controlled text through MCP or collaborative channels into n8n
mitigations: Add strict provenance tags to all TREK-originated content
Disable automatic prompt ingestion from shared files
Require human review before n8n uses TREK text as instructions
Restrict MCP tools to read-only for TREK content
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing

B_data_leakage.rationale: n8n has broad network egress and handles per-credential secrets on its server; TREK touches API keys, MFA secrets, reservations, and documents. If they share a workspace or workflow, n8n can transmit sensitive TREK data to third-party integrations by default, creating a realistic exfiltration path with sensitive blast radius.
conditions: IF n8n workflows receive TREK reservations, documents, or secrets
IF any n8n integration node forwards that data to an external API
mitigations: Separate TREK secrets from n8n-managed credentials
Block sensitive fields before n8n integration nodes
Use a dedicated redaction step for documents and confirmations
Audit outbound destinations for every workflow
requires-engineering: enforce data-class based egress policy

C_capability_conflict.rationale: n8n can write the server filesystem and spawn subprocesses; TREK is collaborative and stores mutable data in ./data/travel.db and ./uploads/. Overlapping write access to shared mutable resources can corrupt state or overwrite records, and neither profile shows locking or coordination primitives that would prevent conflicts.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same host filesystem or database path
IF concurrent workflows modify TREK files without external locking
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate writable directory
Serialize writes through one orchestrator queue
Back up ./data/travel.db before shared runs
Disable n8n file writes to TREK paths
requires-engineering: add file/database locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n is an automation orchestrator that can act on workflow outputs, while TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in. If n8n consumes TREK outputs as authoritative travel facts, it can propagate errors into bookings, messages, or other downstream actions. The pairwise interaction is undocumented, so the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF n8n uses TREK-generated itineraries or recommendations without verification
IF downstream n8n nodes trigger emails, reservations, or database updates
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any action node
Require source citations for TREK-derived facts
Limit n8n to draft-only outputs from TREK
Add approval gates for bookings and notifications
requires-engineering: implement confidence-aware routing

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles API keys, MFA secrets, reservations, and user accounts, while n8n stores per-credential secrets and can send data to many integrations. If TREK data flows into n8n workflows, retention and residency controls may diverge, creating a compliance mismatch. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction breach, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF TREK personal data is processed by n8n workflows with different retention settings
IF any workflow exports EU or regulated data to external integrations
mitigations: Document data-class handling for both systems
Align retention settings for logs and uploads
Exclude secrets from n8n workflow inputs
Review residency of every external integration
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated data
